title: finding(components/types): the shipped `tabs` defaultProps emits items that FAIL the published `TabItemSchema` — every item spells `body` and omits the required `content`
body:
The shipped `tabs` registration's `defaultProps` emits tab items that **fail the published `TabItemSchema`**. Seat-verified at source on `origin/main` **00c4df509**.

```tsx
// packages/components/src/renderers/layout/tabs.tsx, defaultProps.items
{ label: 'Tab 1', value: 'tab1', body: [{ type: 'text', content: 'Content for Tab 1' }] },
{ label: 'Tab 2', value: 'tab2', body: [...] },
{ label: 'Tab 3', value: 'tab3', body: [...] },
```

```ts
// packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts:420
export const TabItemSchema = z.object({
  value: z.string()…, label: z.string()…, icon: …optional(), disabled: …optional(),
  content: z.union([SchemaNodeSchema, z.array(SchemaNodeSchema)]).describe('Tab content'),   // :425 — REQUIRED
});
```

⇒ the item face declares **`content`, required**, and declares **no `body` at all**. The default an author drops into their canvas therefore parses as `invalid_type ["content"] expected nonoptional, received undefined` — measured by the objectui#9871 dev against the **built** schema, with the lit control in the same command: the same item spelled `content` parses green with keys `value,label,content`.

## Class (b) — it violates a contract this repository publishes

⛔ Not a style question and ⛔ not the `body`-vs-`children` dialect question: whatever that family is ruled to be, **this item is invalid against its own published schema today**. The key it carries is dropped by the parse and the key the parse requires is absent.

## ⭐ Why it is filed apart from the dialect family

`TabItem`'s canonical child key is **`content`**, ⛔ not `children` — so objectui#6771's remedy (「`children` is the one spelling」) names a key the item face does not have, and objectui#6771 step 3 (retire `body` from the published type) has **no subject** here because the published item type never declared `body`. ⇒ the family question is live and belongs to objectui#9871; **this** card does not wait on it. Fixing it is spelling the shipped default the way its own schema declares, whichever way that question is ruled.

⚠️ What this card does ⛔ NOT assert: that the rendered UI is broken. The renderer reads `item.body` through an `any` cast, so the default draws; it is the **declared** contract that refuses it. The user-visible cost is an author who copies the shipped default into authored metadata and gets a refusal from a validator that the platform's own sample does not satisfy.

## Dedupe words

`tab item defaultProps fails TabItemSchema` · `tabs shipped default missing required content` · `item face body undeclared` · `defaultProps invalid against published schema` · `TabItem content required`
